q: The number of perfect square numbers between 50 and 1000 is = ?
s: The first perfect square number after 50 is 64 $$\left( {64 = {8^2}} \right)$$ and the last perfect square number before 1000 is 961 $$\left[ {961 = {{\left( {31} \right)}^2}} \right]$$ So, the perfect squares between 50 and 1000 are the squares of numbers from 8 to 31. (31 - 8) + 1 = 24 Clearly, these are 24 in number.

s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \sqrt {x + \frac{x}{y}} = x\sqrt {\frac{x}{y}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x + \frac{x}{y} = {x^2}.\frac{x}{y} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{xy + x}}{y} = \frac{{{x^3}}}{y} \\ & \Leftrightarrow xy + x = {x^3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow y + 1 = {x^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = {x^2} - 1 \end{aligned}$$

One-fourth of a herd of camels was seen in the forest. Twice the square root of the herd had gone to mountains and the remaining 15 camels were seen on the bank of a river. Find the total number of camels ?
s: Let the total number of camels be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow x - \left( {\frac{x}{4} + 2\sqrt x } \right) = 15 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{3x}}{4} - 2\sqrt x = 15 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3x - 8\sqrt x = 60 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 8\sqrt x = 3x - 60 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 64x = {\left( {3x - 60} \right)^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 64x = 9{x^2} + 3600 - 360x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9{x^2} - 424x + 3600 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9{x^2} - 324x - 100x + 3600 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 9x\left( {x - 36} \right) - 100\left( {x - 36} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 36} \right)\left( {9x - 100} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 36\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\because x \ne \frac{{100}}{9}} \right] \end{aligned}$$
